what_it_does: Modern chips often contain a Neural Processing Unit (NPU — a dedicated chip area built to run AI models fast) shared by multiple AI models running at the same time, called multi-tenant execution. When models share the NPU, they also compete for the same on-chip cache (a small, very fast scratchpad memory sitting right next to the compute units), and that competition slows everything down. This paper studies how cache contention hurts multi-tenant NPU workloads — an area the authors say has not been carefully analyzed before. Their solution pairs lightweight extra hardware that can carve out private cache regions for each model with a scheduling strategy that decides how much cache each tenant gets as their demands shift at runtime. The combined approach is said to improve performance by reducing the interference between concurrently running models, though the specific gains come from the full paper rather than the abstract.
